title: Spending policies: who and what can consume Copilot Credits, and up to how much
summary: The page passes: the administrative paths, Graph operations, spending rules and licensing statements are supported by Microsoft documentation. A minor clarification is needed because Microsoft's monitoring documentation gives conflicting descriptions of user-level policy history.

claims.claim: Default spending policy activation starts at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Get Started.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot and then the Cost Management node. To unlock AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing, select Get Started.

claims.claim: Identity policy creation is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Identity.
claims.quote: Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy. ... Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates identity-based spending policies.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies

claims.claim: Policy settings can be changed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy > Save changes.
claims.quote: Select the Configuration tab. Select the spending policy you want to edit. ... After making the necessary changes, select Save changes to apply the updates to the spending policy.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates the policy properties specified in the row's limiting note.
claims.quote: PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} ... The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.claim: Policy alerts are at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy > Alerts, and Email alert settings.
claims.quote: Select the spending policy you want to edit. The spending policy details fly-out opens, where you can modify its settings. This includes: ... Alerts, and Email alert settings

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/emailThresholdSettings configures policy alert thresholds.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. ... Update costManagementAlertSetting | PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/emailThresholdSettings | Create or update the alert configuration.

claims.claim: Resource policy creation starts at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Resources.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. Select Configuration, and then select Add spending policy. Enter a name for the policy, then select Resources as its scope.

claims.claim: Policies can be removed at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > More actions next to the policy > Delete.
claims.quote: Select the Configuration tab. ... Select the More actions menu (⋮) next to the spending policy. Select Delete.

claims.claim: DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} removes a spending policy.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. ... Delete spendingPolicy | DELETE /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} | Delete a spending policy.

claims.claim: An administrator-defined spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center governs who or which resources can consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Administrators can use the dashboard to: Configure identity and resource-based spending policies. Control which users and groups can access supported services using identity-based policies. Set spending limits for supported users, environments, and agents.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Spending policies can cap monthly Copilot Credit consumption.
claims.quote: Limited monthly budget: When you select a limited monthly budget, you limit the number of credits that this policy can spend each month.

claims.claim: A spending policy selects the billing method against which its covered services consume credits.
claims.quote: Use the check box to select the agents and services that can consume credits against the billing method tied to this policy.

claims.claim: Spending policies do not reserve credits for users or groups.
claims.quote: Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.

claims.where: What it is; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Spending policies do not allocate or purchase credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies only define access and spending limits, not credit allocation. ... Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Identity-based policies follow the person using selected services.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want a policy to apply to the people who use selected agents and services.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Identity-based policies can target all users or specific groups.
claims.quote: By default, All users is selected. To target this rule to a subset of users, switch to Specific groups and select the directory group. You can also select multiple groups.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Identity-based policies support a per-user limit.
claims.quote: Select monthly budget limits for users (optional). ... Specify the maximum credit limit users can spend per month.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Resource-based policies follow the agent or environment rather than the user's identity.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want usage to follow an agent or environment rather than the identity of the person using it.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy; controls[4]
claims.claim: Resource policies can target specific agents, specific environments or all environments.
claims.quote: Choose what the policy covers: Specific resources ... Specific environments ... All environments

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy; controls[4]
claims.claim: Resource-based policies support per-agent limits.
claims.quote: You can also set a per-agent limit so that no single agent covered by the policy uses more than the amount you specify.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Identity-based policies apply to groups using Cowork.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want a policy to apply to the people who use selected agents and services. For example, a group using Cowork.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Resource-based spending policies are documented for Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Manage Copilot Studio spending in the Microsoft 365 admin center by creating policies for environments or individual agents.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: An identity-based spending policy cannot be converted into a resource-based one.
claims.quote: You can't convert an existing identity-based policy into a resource-based policy.

claims.quote: The default setup targets your entire organization and all users.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Activating the default policy unlocks experiences gated by usage-based billing.
claims.quote: This process activates AI experiences, like Cowork, that are gated by usage-based billing.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Additional policies have independent limits and do not inherit the tenant-level limit.
claims.quote: Each additional spending policy that you create has its own independent limit and doesn't inherit the tenant-level limit.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; controls[2].ui
claims.claim: A policy contains selected agents and services that administrators can edit.
claims.quote: The spending policy details fly-out opens, where you can modify its settings. This includes: Scope; Agents and services; Billing method; Spending limits; Alerts, and Email alert settings

claims.where: What it is: How it works; controls[2].ui
claims.claim: A policy can contain a monthly policy-level spending limit.
claims.quote: Select the monthly spending limit for this policy.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits: Auto-apply
claims.claim: Auto-apply new services is on by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Auto-apply new services toggle is selected for spending policies.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits: Auto-apply; What to check
claims.claim: Auto-apply automatically adds future supported services and agents; turning it off requires manual review and addition.
claims.quote: When the setting is on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy. When the setting is off, future services and agents aren't automatically included. Administrators must review and add the new services and agents to the policy.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits: Overlapping policies; What to check
claims.claim: For a user in multiple policies for the same service, the highest per-user limit wins.
claims.quote: If a user is in more than one policy for the same service, the system assigns the user a policy based on the following order: 1. Highest per-user limit

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A tie in per-user limits is resolved by the largest overall policy limit.
claims.quote: If tied, the largest overall policy limit

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A remaining tie is resolved by the most recently created policy.
claims.quote: If still tied, the most recently created policy

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: When a per-user limit is not set, the overall policy limit is used as the per-user comparison value.
claims.quote: If a policy doesn't have a per-user limit set, the system uses its overall policy limit as the per-user value for this comparison.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits: Overlapping policies
claims.claim: The selected policy applies in full rather than combining settings or limits from overlapping policies.
claims.quote: The chosen policy applies in full and settings from other policies aren't combined.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: For covered Copilot Studio usage, Microsoft 365 admin center policies take precedence over Power Platform admin center controls.
claims.quote: If a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center covers the environment or agent, its controls take precedence over the Power Platform admin center controls for that usage.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Within the Microsoft 365 admin center, resource-based Copilot Studio policies take precedence over identity-based policies.
claims.quote: Resource-based policy before identity-based policy. Within the Microsoft 365 admin center, a policy for the agent or its environment takes precedence over a policy for the person using the agent.

claims.claim: Initial usage-based billing setup includes activating the default policy before creating additional policies.
claims.quote: Before you create additional spending policies, complete the initial usage-based billing setup and activate the default spending policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends configuring a per-user limit to prevent runaway credit spending by one individual.
claims.quote: Although this selection is optional, review and set this option for your organization to prevent runaway spending of Copilot Credits by one individual user.

claims.claim: Don't limit monthly spending permits usage against the billing method without a policy-level monthly ceiling.
claims.quote: Don't limit monthly spending - Allows the policy to use credits against the organization's billing method without restrictions.

claims.claim: Resource-based Copilot Studio spending management is opt-in, with existing Power Platform configuration continuing until a policy covers the scope.
claims.quote: To opt in, create a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy. Until then, your existing Power Platform admin center configuration remains in effect.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[4].note; Risks and limits: All environments
claims.claim: Covered resource scopes stop using their Power Platform admin center capacity allocations.
claims.quote: For resources covered by the spending policy, Copilot Credit management moves to the Microsoft 365 admin center, replacing their Power Platform admin center capacity allocations and linked billing plans.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Risks and limits: All environments
claims.claim: Covered resource scopes stop using their linked Power Platform admin center billing plans.
claims.quote: Existing Power Platform capacity allocations and linked billing plans don't apply while spending for that environment is managed by a resource-based spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Usage-based billing charges for actual consumption measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Microsoft's usage-based billing model charges customers based on actual usage, measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Credits consumed under a policy are billed to the subscription selected as its billing method.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are billed to the subscription that you select in the billing method.

claims.claim: When credits run out for the selected subscription, usage continues on a pay-as-you-go basis.
claims.quote: When credits run out for that subscription, usage automatically continues on a pay-as-you-go basis.

claims.claim: When both prepaid capacity packs and an Azure subscription with Copilot P3 are selected, funding order is capacity packs, P3, then pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: If you select both Prepaid Capacity packs and an Azure subscription with Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3), billing is applied in the following order ... Prepaid Capacity packs; Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3); Pay-as-you-go billing

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls: Roles
claims.claim: Global administrators and Billing administrators can choose different policy billing methods for departmental billing.
claims.quote: If you're a Global administrator or a Billing administrator, you can override this selection and select how this policy should be billed. This feature enables you to do departmental billing and vary billing methods for each group, department, or set of users.

claims.claim: Licensing requirements depend on the service covered by the policy.
claims.quote: Depending on the service, organizations can use fixed licensing, the Copilot Credit Pre-purchase Plan (P3), pay-as-you-go billing, prepaid capacity packs, or supported combinations of these billing methods.

claims.claim: Cowork requires a Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Cowork (Copilot license required)

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions: credit rates
claims.claim: The spending-policy pages do not state per-service credit rates and direct readers to the Copilot Credits licensing guide.
claims.quote: Searched: "spending policies" "credit rates". Read setup, manage credits, Studio costs, usage-based billing overview and monitor spending: no per-service rate table; overview points to https://aka.ms/CopilotCredits/LicensingGuide for licensing details.

claims.claim: The Consumption tab shows estimated cost that might not match the bill.
claims.quote: Cost: The estimated cost of your AI usage in local currency, including negotiated rates. It includes usage paid for with prepaid credits and with pay-as-you-go, so it might not match your bill.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit; Governance controls: Interaction
claims.claim: Users who hit a spending limit lose access to covered agents and services.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit
claims.claim: The monthly limit resets on the first of the month, restoring the monthly allowance.
claims.quote: For the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit; Governance controls: Watching
claims.claim: Users who reach their policy limit can request more credits.
claims.quote: When users reach their limit within a policy, they can request more credits but they don't default to other policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit
claims.claim: Reaching a user policy limit does not trigger fallback to another policy.
claims.quote: The system keeps the user on the assigned policy and doesn't reevaluate the user against other policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: A running task can complete even when it exceeds a per-user spending limit.
claims.quote: Users in a group spending policy that exceed their per-user spending limit: If a running task exceeds the per-user limit, it can complete without interruption.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: The task's excess per-user usage does not count toward the policy limit.
claims.quote: The excess usage doesn't count toward the policy limit

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun; Open questions: excess billing
claims.claim: Microsoft describes excess per-user task usage as not billed at Microsoft's sole discretion.
claims.quote: Isn't billed (at Microsoft's sole discretion)

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: Excess per-user task usage does not appear as consumed credits in Cost Management dashboards.
claims.quote: Doesn't appear as consumed credits in the Cost Management dashboards (Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management).

claims.where: Risks and limits: All environments; What to check
claims.claim: All environments makes resource-based spending management apply tenant-wide, including new environments.
claims.quote: All environments: All existing environments and automatically includes new environments.

claims.where: Risks and limits: All environments; Open questions: timing
claims.claim: After an environment is linked, a newly created resource-based policy can take up to 12 minutes to apply.
claims.quote: When you create a policy: After you link an environment to a Microsoft 365 spending policy, allow up to 12 minutes for the new policy to apply.

claims.claim: Removing an environment or deleting its resource-based policy automatically restores the applicable Power Platform policy.
claims.quote: If you remove an environment from a spending policy or delete the resource-based spending policy, the applicable Power Platform admin center policy resumes for that environment automatically.

claims.claim: Resource-based policies do not apply to AI Builder features or their credit consumption.
claims.quote: Resource-based policies created in the Microsoft 365 admin center don't apply to AI Builder features or the credits they consume.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises against moving resources that use AI Builder into resource-based spending policies.
claims.quote: Don't move resources, agents, workflows or environments that use AI Builder to these policies.

claims.claim: Moving users between groups does not reset consumption; earlier usage counts when enforcing the new policy's limit.
claims.quote: Credits consumed under the previous spending policy remain part of the user's consumption history and are accounted for when enforcing the spending limit under the new policy. Moving a user between groups or spending policies doesn't reset the user's consumption.

claims.claim: After a group move, the Consumption tab shows only current usage against the current policy at user level.
claims.quote: Only the current usage against the current spending policy is displayed at a user level in the Consumption tab view.
claims.fix: Add after this sentence: 'Microsoft's monitoring page also says the Users details panel shows spending policy history and credits spent by policy for the past month; the usage-based billing overview likewise describes daily usage and credits spent by policy, so the documentation is inconsistent about this view.' Both pages are already cited: https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-copilot-credits-monitor-spending and https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits.
